assumptions: System states require normalization against a noise baseline to distinguish divergent signal.
Internal coupling coefficients modulate state transition regimes.
The baseline noise model is independent of the coupling mechanism.
definition.falsification: If the normalized divergence ratio remains < 0.2 across a wider variance of coupling conditions, the hypothesis that value divergence is driven primarily by coupling sensitivity is falsified.
definition.statement: Intelligent systems exhibit detectable path-dependent value divergence when internal coupling coefficients exceed a critical threshold, relative to a noise-baseline. The divergence ratio is therefore a function of the system's sensitivity to perturbation, normalized against stochastic variance. If observed divergence remains low, it suggests the baseline noise model is not independent of the coupling mechanism.
definition.uncertainty: Normalization methods against stochastic noise may inadvertently mask true divergence; we are adjusting the target threshold and exploring the coupling/noise relationship.

definition.method: Execute a modified sensitivity sweep on coupling coefficients (range 0.1 to 1.0) with reduced noise variance injection to isolate signal.
definition.source: def experiment(inputs): import random; params = inputs.get('parameters', {}); seeds = inputs.get('seeds', [1, 2, 3]); random.seed(seeds[0]); coupling = params.get('coupling', 0.5); baseline = [random.random() for _ in range(10)]; trajectory_a = [x * coupling + (random.random() * 0.05) for x in baseline]; trajectory_b = [x * coupling + (random.random() * 0.05) for x in baseline]; diff = sum(abs(a - b) for a, b in zip(trajectory_a, trajectory_b)); return {'divergence_ratio_internal_state': diff / sum(baseline)}
definition.stop: If three consecutive sweeps across 0.1-1.0 yield values < 0.05.
definition.success: Measured divergence ratio meets or exceeds 0.2.

definition.reason: Previous empirical results were inconclusive. Re-calibrating the sensitivity sweep with refined noise baselines is required to test the hypothesis validity.
definition.stop: Experiment rejection or clear threshold crossing.
definition.uncertainty: High; the divergence signal remains weak.

proposal.summary: The previous experiment (exp-divergent-values-test-91) failed to reach the target divergence threshold of 0.3, yielding 0.028. This suggests the coupling coefficient of 0.95 or the noise baseline normalization may be masking divergence. A revised hypothesis and new experimental protocol will test lower coupling ranges and adjusted noise normalization parameters.
proposal.title: Path Dependence and Divergent Values: Experimental Refinement
